status.en: 141 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 28% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata.

summary.en: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan met top security officials in Jammu to review the situation and discuss anti-infiltration measures, while security forces in Manipur buried seven Kuki civilians killed by militants after two months and shifted the BSF Raising Day parade from Manipur to Delhi over security concerns. In the border region, China and India held fresh talks as both sides increased military readiness before winter. A bear attack injured five people in Udhampur and a leopard injured a seven-year-old boy in Kupwara shortly after a fatal attack in the same district. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Unionens innenriksminister Govind Mohan møtte topp sikkerhetsoffiserer i Jammu for å gjennomgå situasjonen og diskutere anti-inntrengings-tiltak, mens sikkerhetsstyrkene i Manipur begravde syv Kuki-sivile drept av militante etter to måneder og flyttet BSF-sitt-dag-paraden fra Manipur til Delhi på grunn av sikkerhetsbekymringer. I grenseområdet holdt Kina og India friske samtaler mens begge sider økte militær beredskap før vinteren. Et bjørnangrep såret fem personer i Udhampur og en leopard såret en syv år gammel gutt i Kupwara kort tid etter et dødelig angrep i samme distrikt. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
